content: Ethacridine lactate is an aromatic organic compound derived from acridine. It is also known by the synonyms acrinol, rivanol, and ethacridine monolactate monohydrate. Its formal chemical name is 2-ethoxy-6,9-diaminoacridine monolactate monohydrate. This compound appears as orange-yellow crystals and has a melting point of 226°C. It emits a distinctive stinging odor. Ethacridine is utilized as an agent for second-trimester abortion. A 1% solution of ethacridine lactate is administered extra-amniotically via a Foley catheter. Following this procedure, uterine contractions, often referred to as mini labor, typically occur within 20 to 40 hours. In China, an intra-amniotic method of administration has also been employed. When used as an abortifacient, ethacridine has been found to be safer and better tolerated compared to the use of 20% hypertonic saline solutions.
